items.name: Claude Fable 5.2
items.summary: Anthropic's most capable model to date, released November 9 with a 1M-token context window, output up to 30% faster than Fable 5.1, and pricing 20% lower at $8/$40 per million tokens. It took first place on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, while the same underlying model ships as the restricted Mythos 5.2 for verified cybersecurity and life-sciences organisations.

items.name: Meta Muse Ember
items.summary: Meta's smallest and cheapest Muse model, launched November 9 for the repetitive work agents do all day — tool calls, coding subtasks, routing, extraction and long-document parsing. At $0.10 per million input tokens it matches Claude Haiku 5.5's benchmark score at about a third of the cost per task, with a 1M-token context window.

items.name: NVIDIA GR00T 2
items.summary: An open robot foundation model unveiled November 9 at the Conference on Robot Learning, built on NVIDIA Cosmos to learn dexterous manipulation largely by watching human video. NVIDIA reports 95% average success across 50 tasks after five demonstrations each, and is releasing 100,000 hours of human training video openly; model code is due in December.

items.name: Thinking Machines Inkling 2 Small
items.summary: Thinking Machines Lab's second-generation model, announced November 5: a 594-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 17 billion active parameters per token, multimodal input and a 1M-token context. It is available now through the company's Tinker platform, with full weights promised under Apache 2.0 next week once external safety testing finishes.

items.name: OpenAI GPT-Image-2.6
items.summary: OpenAI's Images 2.6, released November 4 in ChatGPT, Codex and the API, generates images 50% faster and adds animated GIF output, SVG export and markup-guided edits. Developers get two API models — Flare for fast iteration (as little as six seconds per image) and Sunburst for detailed, consistent edits — at unchanged 2.5-generation pricing.
